rule: Every contract's awardID matches an award in the same process
formalise_as: OWL: basedOnAward functional, Contract exactly 1 Award + SHACL sh:class

rule: Every award supplier is a party with the role supplier
Every buyer is a party with the role buyer
notes: 8 processes have no buyer_id at all

rule: Every award has at least one supplier
formalise_as: OWL: Award subClassOf awardedTo some Organization + SHACL sh:minCount 1
notes: Open world (OWL) vs closed world (SHACL) example

rule: tender_numberOfTenderers equals the number of tender_tenderers rows
formalise_as: SHACL/SPARQL count check (counting is not an OWL strength)

rule: Every award has a contract
notes: Cancelled, pending or missing data? see award status

rule: A complete tender has at least one award
A cancelled tender has no award
Tenders with status planning or unsuccessful never have an award
formalise_as: OWL: PlanningTender, UnsuccessfulTender subClassOf not (resultsInAward some Award)

rule: An active contract never sits on a cancelled award
A contract with status 'terminated' sits on an active award
formalise_as: OWL: ClosedContract (code 'terminated' = ran and ended, NOT failed); SHACL: exactly one status class
notes: Read as English, 'terminated' sounds like failure. In OCDS it means closed. Broken here = terminated contracts whose award is NOT active

rule: Tender period starts before it ends
An award is dated on or after the tender period ends
A contract is signed on or after its award date
formalise_as: SHACL SPARQL constraint, severity Warning (triage the gaps)
notes: Many gaps are under a day: dateSigned is stored at 12:00, award date with a real time

rule: Contract period starts before it ends
Total awarded value is at most the tender value
formalise_as: SHACL SPARQL constraint (needs SUM), severity Warning

rule: Contract value equals its award value
notes: Every contract has exactly 1 award; DNCP copies the value across

rule: Each process uses a single currency
notes: Currency is not constant: PYG 148403, USD 327

rule: Award and contract amounts are non-negative
One supplier identifier always carries one name
formalise_as: SHACL sh:maxCount 1 on rdfs:label of Organization

rule: One normalised supplier name always carries one identifier
formalise_as: Mapping + entity resolution (Step 2): owl:sameAs only when the IDs agree
notes: Do not merge on name alone: same name can be two people

rule: Direct contracting means at most one tenderer
formalise_as: Not a rule: the method name does not imply one bidder (ontology note on the method)

rule: Each procurement method label appears in one spelling
